case_title: Parteek Bansal v. State of Rajasthan & Ors.
aggravating_circumstances: Abuse of process of law, harassment, misuse of official position
neutral_facts: The accused, a Chartered Accountant, was married to the victim, who was a Deputy Superintendent of Police. The complainant, the victim's father, filed a complaint against the accused at the Police Station in Hisar, Haryana, on 10.10.2015, alleging offences under Sections 498A and 34 of the IPC. A second complaint was filed at the Police Station in Udaipur, Rajasthan, on 15.10.2015, with the same allegations and additional information about the earlier complaint. The first FIR was registered on 17.10.2015, and the second FIR was registered on 01.11.2015. The investigation in Hisar led to the trial court acquitting the accused. The High Court dismissed the quashing petition of the FIR in Udaipur, but the Supreme Court found that the complainant and the victim's conduct constituted an abuse of the process of law, as they did not withdraw the first complaint or appear before the trial court, indicating an intention to harass the accused.
